tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

schema.name: SendUserFile
schema.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# Company Leadership RAG Agent

Given a company domain, collects its leadership (C-level, VPs, Heads) from
public sources into a verifiable SQLite dataset, and answers questions over it
through an LLM chat.

Status: **M0** (project setup) and **M1** (database schema, role resolution
rules) and **M2** (finding and fetching sources) are done and accepted.
**M3** (extracting people and roles from the sources) is done and accepted.
**M4** (verification, location and biography, export, measurement) is done and accepted;
its recall limits are listed below.
**M5** (the chat agent, command line) is built. The web UI is not built yet. See [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) for
the design, `SPEC_checklist.xlsx` for the requirement checklist, and
`acceptance/` for each milestone's test results.

## Setup

Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```bash
uv sync
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in at least one of `OPENAI_API_KEY` or
`GROQ_API_KEY`. Then verify the keys:

```bash
uv run leadership check
```

"""Streamlit chat over the collected leadership data. SPEC section 5, "UI".

    uv run streamlit run app.py

Reads the committed fixtures (fixtures/leadership.db); needs one LLM key in
.env and no collection step. Each answer has a panel with the SQL that ran
and the rows it returned.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

import streamlit as st

from leadership.agent import Agent
from leadership.citations import add_missing_sources
from leadership.config import ROOT, ConfigError, configured_providers, load_config, load_env

FIXTURE = ROOT / "fixtures" / "leadership.db"
EXAMPLES = ["Who is the CEO?", "Who are the current C-level executives?",
            "How many C-level executives were found?", "Who was the previous CFO?"]


def companies() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(domain, name) of the companies in the fixtures, read by this page, not by the model."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{FIXTURE.as_posix()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        return conn.execute("SELECT domain, name FROM companies ORDER BY name").fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()

\[REDACTED]_resource(show_spinner=False)
def agent_for(domain: str) -> Agent:
    return Agent(load_config(), domain, FIXTURE)


def rows_table(columns: list[str], rows: list[list]) -> str:
    """The rows as a plain Markdown table. Not st.dataframe: that needs pyarrow's compiled libraries,
    which some machines' security policy blocks."""
    def cell(value) -> str:
        text = "" if value is None else str(value)
        text = text if len(text) <= 160 else text[:157] + "..."
        return text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ").replace("$", "\\$")

    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(columns)]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(cell(v) for v in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def show_answer(entry: dict) -> None:
    text = entry["text"].replace("$", "\\$")           # a dollar sign is not the start of a formula
    if entry["ok"]:
        st.markdown(text)
    else:
        st.error(text)
    with st.expander("SQL and source rows"):
        if not entry["steps"]:
            st.caption("No query ran.")
        for i, step in enumerate(entry["steps"], 1):
            st.code(step.sql or "(empty)", language="sql")
            if step.error:
                st.caption(f"Query {i} was refused or failed: {step.error}")
            elif step.rows:
                st.markdown(rows_table(step.columns, step.rows))
            else:
                st.caption(f"Query {i} returned no rows.")
        st.caption("Answered from the cache." if entry["cached"] else f"Model: {entry['model']}")


def main() -> None:
    st.set_page_config(page_title="Company leadership", page_icon=":material/groups:")
    load_env()
    st.title("Company leadership")
    if not FIXTURE.exists():
        st.error("No data found at fixtures/leadership.db. Run `uv run leadership export` first.")
        return
    options = companies()
    if not options:
        st.error("The database holds no company. Run `uv run leadership collect` and `export` first.")
        return
    with st.sidebar:
        domain = st.selectbox("Company", [d for d, _ in options],
                              format_func=lambda d: dict(options)[d] + f" ({d})")
        st.caption("Answers come only from public sources collected for this company. Each answer has a "
                   "panel with the SQL that ran and the rows behind it.")
        st.markdown("**Try:**\n" + "\n".join(f"- {q}" for q in EXAMPLES))
    if not configured_providers():
        st.error("No LLM key found. Copy .env.example to .env and set GROQ_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, then "
                 "reload this page.")
        return
    try:
        agent = agent_for(domain)
    except ConfigError as e:
        st.error(f"Configuration problem: {e}")
        return
    if agent.status != "complete":
        st.warning(f"The data collection for this company did not finish normally (status {agent.status}). "
                   "Answers are based on partial data.")
    history: list[dict] = st.session_state.setdefault(f"history:{domain}", [])
    for entry in history:
        with st.chat_message("user"):
            st.markdown(entry["question"])
        with st.chat_message("assistant"):
            show_answer(entry)
    question = st.chat_input(f"Ask about {agent.company}'s leadership")
    if question:
        with st.chat_message("user"):
            st.markdown(question)
        with st.chat_message("assistant"):
            with st.spinner("Looking it up in the collected data..."):
                result = agent.ask(question)
            entry = {"question": question, "text": add_missing_sources(result.text, result.steps),
                     "ok": result.ok, "steps": result.steps, "cached": result.cached, "model": result.model}
            show_answer(entry)
        history.append(entry)


main()

# M6 acceptance report: Streamlit UI

- **Run date:** 2026-11-13
- **Branch:** `m6-ui`, branched from `m5-chat` (`bfd017f`), so it includes M5,
  which is not merged yet. The log was captured before the M6 commit.
- **Raw evidence:** [M6_results.log](M6_results.log) — full, unedited command output
- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M6`
- **Needs:** one LLM key. The one question in the tests is answered from the
  M5 cache, so the stage made no model call.

## 1. Automated results

All numbers below are copied from `M6_results.log`.

| # | Step | Expected | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | M6 tests (no key) | all pass | 2 passed: both companies listed from the fixtures; without a key the page says what to do and shows no chat box | PASS |
| 2 | Whole fast suite | all pass | 360 passed, 16 deselected (the 16 need keys) | PASS |
| 3 | Real-model page test | pass | 1 passed: "Who is the CEO?" for Robinhood shows Tenev with a URL; the panel holds the SQL on `current_leadership` and a table of rows; switching to Campfire shows Campfire's own, empty history | PASS |
| 4 | Secret scan | 0 problems | 252 files scanned, 0 problems | PASS |

4 of 4 steps as expected.

I also opened the page in a browser, chose Robinhood, and asked "Who is the
CEO?". The answer named Vladimir Tenev with the SEC URL, and the panel showed
the SQL and one row, with "Answered from the cache."

## 2. M6 acceptance criteria (SPEC section 8)

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Runs from committed fixtures with one LLM key | Met | The page reads only `fixtures/leadership.db`; no collection step (steps 1, 3) |
| Shows the answer, SQL and sources | Met | Step 3 and the browser check |
| A fresh clone works | Not tested here; it is the M7 fresh-clone test | |

## 3. What the page does

`app.py`, one file, about 120 lines:

- **Sidebar:** a company selector (the companies in the fixtures) and the
  four sample questions as a hint.
- **Chat:** each company keeps its own history for the browser session. An
  answer goes through the M5 agent unchanged, including the sources appended
  from the queried rows.
- **Panel under each answer**, "SQL and source rows": every query that ran,
  its rows as a table, or why it failed or returned nothing, and whether the
  answer came from the cache.
- **Incomplete data:** if the company's run status is not `complete`, a
  warning above the chat says the answers are based on partial data.
- **No key:** an error that says how to add one; no chat box.
- **Model failure:** the agent's error message is shown as an error, not as
  an answer.

## 4. Issues met during M6

| # | What happened | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `st.dataframe` failed to load | This machine's Windows application control policy blocks pyarrow's compiled library | The rows are shown as a Markdown table, which needs no pyarrow. The policy was not changed or worked around |
| 2 | `uv run streamlit run app.py` was refused | The same policy blocks the `streamlit.exe` launcher | Run it as `uv run python -m streamlit run app.py`. That works everywhere, so it is the documented command |

## 5. Decisions made during M6 that the spec did not fix

Please confirm or change these in MT-6.6.

1. **Markdown tables instead of `st.dataframe`** (issue 1). The tables cannot
   be sorted, but long cells are cut at 160 characters.
2. **History is per company and per browser session.** It is not saved, and
   reloading the page clears it.
3. **The sample questions in the sidebar are a hint only.** They cannot be
   clicked. That would be a little more code and is not in the spec.

## 6. Limitations

- Everything in M5's limitations applies, because the page uses the same agent.
- Fresh-clone use is tested only in M7.
- I checked the page in one browser at desktop width, not on a phone.

## 7. Manual acceptance tests

Run these in a terminal opened in the project folder. Only MT-6.4 asks a new
question; the others use cached answers.

- [ ] **MT-6.1 Tests.** `uv run pytest tests/test_app.py -m "llm or not llm"`
  Expected: `3 passed`.

- [ ] **MT-6.2 Start the page.** `uv run python -m streamlit run app.py`
  Expected: a browser tab opens at http://localhost:8501 with the title
  "Company leadership" and a "Company" selector in the sidebar that lists
  Campfire and Robinhood. (Stop it later with Ctrl+C in the terminal.)

- [ ] **MT-6.3 A sample question.** Choose Robinhood and ask "Who was the
  previous CFO?".
  Expected: Jason Warnick, effective 2026-02-06, with the SEC URL. Open
  "SQL and source rows": the SQL reads `leadership`, there is a table of rows,
  and the panel says "Answered from the cache."

- [ ] **MT-6.4 Your own question (one real model call or a few).** Choose
  Campfire and ask something not in the evaluation, for example "Who leads
  engineering?".
  Expected: an answer only from the data, or "not found", with a source URL
  for every person named; the panel shows "Model: ..." instead of the cache
  line.

- [ ] **MT-6.5 Switching company.** Switch back to Robinhood.
  Expected: your Robinhood question is still there, and the Campfire one is
  not. The chat box says "Ask about Robinhood's leadership".

- [ ] **MT-6.6 Decisions.** Read section 5; confirm or change.

- [ ] **MT-6.7 Checklist.** In `SPEC_checklist.xlsx`, filter Milestone to
  `M6` and review R55 to R57.

## 8. Sign-off

| | |
|---|---|
| Manual tests passed | __ of 7 |
| Decisions you want changed (MT-6.6) | |
| Accepted by / date | |

# M6 acceptance report: Streamlit UI

- **Run date:** 2026-11-13
- **Branch:** `m6-ui`, branched from `m5-chat` (`bfd017f`), so it includes M5,
  which is not merged yet. The log was captured before the M6 commit.
- **Raw evidence:** [M6_results.log](M6_results.log) — full, unedited command output
- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M6`
- **Needs:** one LLM key. The one question in the tests is answered from the
  M5 cache, so the stage made no model call.

## 1. Automated results

All numbers below are copied from `M6_results.log`.

| # | Step | Expected | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | M6 tests (no key) | all pass | 2 passed: both companies listed from the fixtures; without a key the page says what to do and shows no chat box | PASS |
| 2 | Whole fast suite | all pass | 360 passed, 16 deselected (the 16 need keys) | PASS |
| 3 | Real-model page test | pass | 1 passed: "Who is the CEO?" for Robinhood shows Tenev with a URL; the panel holds the SQL on `current_leadership` and a table of rows; switching to Campfire shows Campfire's own, empty history | PASS |
| 4 | Secret scan | 0 problems | 252 files scanned, 0 problems | PASS |

4 of 4 steps as expected.

I also opened the page in a browser, chose Robinhood, and asked "Who is the
CEO?". The answer named Vladimir Tenev with the SEC URL, and the panel showed
the SQL and one row, with "Answered from the cache."

## 2. M6 acceptance criteria (SPEC section 8)

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Runs from committed fixtures with one LLM key | Met | The page reads only `fixtures/leadership.db`; no collection step (steps 1, 3) |
| Shows the answer, SQL and sources | Met | Step 3 and the browser check |
| A fresh clone works | Not tested here; it is the M7 fresh-clone test | |

## 3. What the page does

`app.py`, one file, about 120 lines:

- **Sidebar:** a company selector (the companies in the fixtures) and the
  four sample questions as a hint.
- **Chat:** each company keeps its own history for the browser session. An
  answer goes through the M5 agent unchanged, including the sources appended
  from the queried rows.
- **Panel under each answer**, "SQL and source rows": every query that ran,
  its rows as a table, or why it failed or returned nothing, and whether the
  answer came from the cache.
- **Incomplete data:** if the company's run status is not `complete`, a
  warning above the chat says the answers are based on partial data.
- **No key:** an error that says how to add one; no chat box.
- **Model failure:** the agent's error message is shown as an error, not as
  an answer.

## 4. Issues met during M6

| # | What happened | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `st.dataframe` failed to load | This machine's Windows application control policy blocks pyarrow's compiled library | The rows are shown as a Markdown table, which needs no pyarrow. The policy was not changed or worked around |
| 2 | `uv run streamlit run app.py` was refused | The same policy blocks the `streamlit.exe` launcher | Run it as `uv run python -m streamlit run app.py`. That works everywhere, so it is the documented command |

## 5. Decisions made during M6 that the spec did not fix

Please confirm or change these in MT-6.6.

1. **Markdown tables instead of `st.dataframe`** (issue 1). The tables cannot
   be sorted, but long cells are cut at 160 characters.
2. **History is per company and per browser session.** It is not saved, and
   reloading the page clears it.
3. **The sample questions in the sidebar are a hint only.** They cannot be
   clicked. That would be a little more code and is not in the spec.

## 6. Limitations

- Everything in M5's limitations applies, because the page uses the same agent.
- Fresh-clone use is tested only in M7.
- I checked the page in one browser at desktop width, not on a phone.

- [ ] **MT-6.3 A sample question.** Choose Robinhood and ask "Who was the
  previous CFO?".
  Expected: Jason Warnick, effective 2026-02-06, with the SEC URL. Open

- [ ] **MT-6.5 Switching company.** Switch back to Robinhood.

"""Streamlit chat over the collected leadership data. SPEC section 5, "UI".

    uv run python -m streamlit run app.py

Reads the committed fixtures (fixtures/leadership.db); needs one LLM key in
.env and no collection step. Each answer has a panel with the SQL that ran
and the rows it returned.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

import streamlit as st

from leadership.agent import Agent
from leadership.citations import add_missing_sources
from leadership.config import ROOT, ConfigError, configured_providers, load_config, load_env

FIXTURE = ROOT / "fixtures" / "leadership.db"
EXAMPLES = ["Who is the CEO?", "Who are the current C-level executives?",
            "How many C-level executives were found?", "Who was the previous CFO?"]


def companies() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(domain, name) of the companies in the fixtures, read by this page, not by the model."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{FIXTURE.as_posix()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        return conn.execute("SELECT domain, name FROM companies ORDER BY name").fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()

\[REDACTED]_resource(show_spinner=False)
def agent_for(domain: str) -> Agent:
    return Agent(load_config(), domain, FIXTURE)


def rows_table(columns: list[str], rows: list[list]) -> str:
    """The rows as a plain Markdown table. Not st.dataframe: that needs pyarrow's compiled libraries,
    which some machines' security policy blocks."""
    def cell(value) -> str:
        text = "" if value is None else str(value)
        text = text if len(text) <= 160 else text[:157] + "..."
        return text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ").replace("$", "\\$")

    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(columns)]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(cell(v) for v in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def show_answer(entry: dict) -> None:
    text = entry["text"].replace("$", "\\$")           # a dollar sign is not the start of a formula
    if entry["ok"]:
        st.markdown(text)
    else:
        st.error(text)
    with st.expander("SQL and source rows"):
        if not entry["steps"]:
            st.caption("No query ran.")
        for i, step in enumerate(entry["steps"], 1):
            st.code(step.sql or "(empty)", language="sql")
            if step.error:
                st.caption(f"Query {i} was refused or failed: {step.error}")
            elif step.rows:
                st.markdown(rows_table(step.columns, step.rows))
            else:
                st.caption(f"Query {i} returned no rows.")
        st.caption("Answered from the cache." if entry["cached"] else f"Model: {entry['model']}")


def main() -> None:
    st.set_page_config(page_title="Company leadership", page_icon=":material/groups:")
    load_env()
    st.title("Company leadership")
    if not FIXTURE.exists():
        st.error("No data found at fixtures/leadership.db. Run `uv run leadership export` first.")
        return
    options = companies()
    if not options:
        st.error("The database holds no company. Run `uv run leadership collect` and `export` first.")
        return
    with st.sidebar:
        domain = st.selectbox("Company", [d for d, _ in options],
                              format_func=lambda d: dict(options)[d] + f" ({d})")
        st.caption("Answers come only from public sources collected for this company. Each answer has a "
                   "panel with the SQL that ran and the rows behind it.")
        st.markdown("**Try:**\n" + "\n".join(f"- {q}" for q in EXAMPLES))
    if not configured_providers():
        st.error("No LLM key found. Copy .env.example to .env and set GROQ_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, then "
                 "reload this page.")
        return
    try:
        agent = agent_for(domain)
    except ConfigError as e:
        st.error(f"Configuration problem: {e}")
        return
    if agent.status != "complete":
        st.warning(f"The data collection for this company did not finish normally (status {agent.status}). "
                   "Answers are based on partial data.")
    history: list[dict] = st.session_state.setdefault(f"history:{domain}", [])
    for entry in history:
        with st.chat_message("user"):
            st.markdown(entry["question"])
        with st.chat_message("assistant"):
            show_answer(entry)
    question = st.chat_input(f"Ask about {agent.company}'s leadership")
    if question:
        with st.chat_message("user"):
            st.markdown(question)
        with st.chat_message("assistant"):
            with st.spinner("Looking it up in the collected data..."):
                result = agent.ask(question)
            entry = {"question": question, "text": add_missing_sources(result.text, result.steps),
                     "ok": result.ok, "steps": result.steps, "cached": result.cached, "model": result.model}
            show_answer(entry)
        history.append(entry)


main()

"""Citations for chat answers, added without a model. SPEC section 5, answering rules.

The model is told to cite a source URL for every person it names, but it
sometimes gives only the source type and date. `add_missing_sources` then
appends the source URL of each named person from the rows the agent actually
queried. It adds nothing that was not in those rows.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata


def plain(text: str) -> str:
    """Lower case, no accents, typographic apostrophes and spaces made plain."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text.replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'"))
    return "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch)).casefold()


def named(answer: str, name: str) -> bool:
    """The answer names this person (by surname, as a whole word)."""
    return re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(plain(name).split()[-1])}\b", plain(answer)) is not None


def add_missing_sources(text: str, steps) -> str:
    """Append "Sources:" lines for named people whose source URL the answer does not give."""
    sources: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str | None, str | None]]] = {}
    for step in steps:
        if step.error or "person" not in step.columns or "source_url" not in step.columns:
            continue
        i, u = step.columns.index("person"), step.columns.index("source_url")
        d = step.columns.index("source_date") if "source_date" in step.columns else None
        t = step.columns.index("source_type") if "source_type" in step.columns else None
        for row in step.rows:
            if row[i] and row[u]:
                entry = (row[u], row[d] if d is not None else None, row[t] if t is not None else None)
                if entry not in sources.setdefault(row[i], []):
                    sources[row[i]].append(entry)
    lines = []
    for person, entries in sources.items():
        if named(text, person) and not any(url in text for url, _, _ in entries):
            url, date, kind = entries[0]
            lines.append(f"- {person}: {url} ({kind or 'source'}, {date or 'date not stated'})")
    if not lines:
        return text
    return text.rstrip() + "\n\nSources:\n" + "\n".join(lines)

"""The chat agent's only way to read data. SPEC section 5, "SQL guard".

Enforced by SQLite itself, not by inspecting the SQL text:

- the agent's database is a snapshot holding only the two views
  `leadership` and `current_leadership`, copied as plain tables when the
  chat starts. The base tables do not exist in it, so they cannot be read.
  (SQLite reports some reads inside the views' subqueries without the
  view's name, so an authorizer on the full database could not tell them
  from a direct read of a base table.)
- the snapshot is opened read-only (`mode=ro`);
- an authorizer allows reading only those two tables; PRAGMA, ATTACH,
  writes, schema changes and transactions are denied;
- one statement per call, at most `row_limit` rows, and a time limit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import tempfile
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

VIEWS = ("leadership", "current_leadership")
_RECURSIVE = getattr(sqlite3, "SQLITE_RECURSIVE", 33)   # WITH RECURSIVE


class GuardError(Exception):
    """The query was refused or failed. The message is safe to show to the model."""


@dataclass
class Result:
    columns: list[str]
    rows: list[tuple]
    truncated: bool                 # more rows existed than the limit


def snapshot(source: str | Path, company_domain: str | None = None) -> Path:
    """Copy the two views into a new database file of their own. Optionally one company only."""
    source = Path(source).resolve()
    if not source.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(source)
    src = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{source.as_posix()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    target = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="exectrace-chat-")) / "chat.db"
    dst = sqlite3.connect(target)
    for view in VIEWS:
        where, args = ("WHERE company_domain = ?", (company_domain,)) if company_domain else ("", ())
        cur = src.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {view} {where}", args)
        columns = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
        dst.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {view} ({', '.join(columns)})")
        dst.executemany(f"INSERT INTO {view} VALUES ({', '.join('?' * len(columns))})", cur.fetchall())
    dst.commit()
    dst.close()
    src.close()
    return target


def open_readonly(source: str | Path, company_domain: str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """A read-only connection to a snapshot of the two views, with an authorizer that admits nothing else."""
    path = snapshot(source, company_domain)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path.as_posix()}?mode=ro", uri=True, check_same_thread=False)

    def authorize(action, arg1, arg2, db_name, trigger):
        if action in (sqlite3.SQLITE_SELECT, sqlite3.SQLITE_FUNCTION, _RECURSIVE):     # reading only
            return sqlite3.SQLITE_OK
        # Only the two view tables exist; other names read are a query's own WITH clauses.
        # SQLite's internal tables (the schema) are refused.
        if action == sqlite3.SQLITE_READ and not (arg1 or "").lower().startswith("sqlite_"):
            return sqlite3.SQLITE_OK
        return sqlite3.SQLITE_DENY                    # the schema, PRAGMA, ATTACH, writes, DDL

    conn.set_authorizer(authorize)
    return conn


def run(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sql: str, *, row_limit: int = 50, timeout_s: float = 5.0) -> Result:
    """Run one SELECT through the guard. Raises GuardError with a short reason."""
    text = (sql or "").strip().rstrip(";").strip()
    if not text:
        raise GuardError("empty query")
    if not sqlite3.complete_statement(text + ";") or _has_second_statement(text):
        raise GuardError("only one statement per call is allowed")
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
    conn.set_progress_handler(lambda: 1 if time.monotonic() > deadline else 0, 10_000)
    try:
        cur = conn.execute(text)
        rows = cur.fetchmany(row_limit + 1)
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:
        message = str(e)
        if "interrupted" in message:
            message = f"the query took longer than {timeout_s:g} seconds"
        elif message.startswith("no such table"):
            message += "; only the tables leadership and current_leadership exist"
        elif "not authorized" in message or "prohibited" in message:
            message = ("not authorized: only SELECT queries on the views leadership and current_leadership "
                       "are allowed")
        raise GuardError(message) from None
    finally:
        conn.set_progress_handler(None, 0)
    columns = [d[0] for d in cur.description or []]
    return Result(columns, [tuple(r) for r in rows[:row_limit]], len(rows) > row_limit)


def _has_second_statement(text: str) -> bool:
    """True if a statement follows the first one. Semicolons inside strings do not count."""
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch == ";" and sqlite3.complete_statement(text[: i + 1]) and text[i + 1:].strip():
            return True
    return False

    c.add_argument("--show-sql", action="store_true", help="print the SQL that ran and the row counts")

    e.add_argument("--chat", action="store_true", help="evaluate the chat agent only (real LLM, cached)")
    x = sub.add_parser("export", help="write fixtures/<domain>.json and fixtures/leadership.db")
    x.add_argument("domains", nargs="+", help="company domains to export, e.g. robinhood.com")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        load_env()

                evals.run_extraction_eval(cfg)
            return evals.run_gold_eval(cfg)
        if args.command == "export":
            from .config import ROOT
            from .export import export
            try:
                written = export(ROOT / "data" / "leadership.db", ROOT / "fixtures", args.domains)

def _rows(conn, sql):
    r = sqlguard.run(conn, sql)
    return Step(sql=sql, columns=r.columns, rows=[list(x) for x in r.rows])


def test_a_person_cited_by_the_source_that_ended_the_role_gets_no_unrelated_source(hood):
    """The previous-CFO answer cited the SEC filing that ended Warnick's role; a 2020 press release
    about another executive's hire was still appended as his source."""
    from leadership.citations import add_missing_sources
    step = _rows(hood, "SELECT person, title, status, ended_on, ended_by_source_url, ended_by_source_date, "
                       "source_url, source_date, source_type FROM leadership WHERE canonical_role = 'CFO'")
    answer = f"The previous CFO was Jason Warnick, effective 2026-02-06, according to a SEC filing: {SEC}"
    assert add_missing_sources(answer, [step]) == answer
    # Named without a URL: the source that ended the role is the one appended, not the old press release.
    added = add_missing_sources("The previous CFO was Jason Warnick.", [step])
    assert f"Jason Warnick: {SEC}" in added and "smedley" not in added


def test_a_shared_surname_alone_does_not_add_the_other_persons_source():
    from leadership.citations import add_missing_sources
    step = Step(sql="x", columns=["person", "source_url"],
                rows=[["Anna Smith", "https://a.example/1"], ["Bob Smith", "https://b.example/2"]])
    text = add_missing_sources("Anna Smith is the CEO.", [step])
    assert "https://a.example/1" in text and "https://b.example/2" not in text
    assert add_missing_sources("Smith is the CEO.", [step]) == "Smith is the CEO."   # ambiguous: add nothing

def test_the_agent_reads_only_the_selected_companys_data(domain, other_person, tmp_path):
    from leadership.agent import Agent
    from leadership.config import load_config
    from leadership.runlog import RunLog
    agent = Agent(load_config(), domain, FIXTURE, llm=object(), log=RunLog(tmp_path / "c.jsonl"))
    for table in ("leadership", "current_leadership"):
        assert sqlguard.run(agent.conn, f"SELECT DISTINCT company_domain FROM {table}").rows == [(domain,)]
        assert not sqlguard.run(agent.conn, f"SELECT 1 FROM {table} WHERE person = '{other_person}'").rows
    other = "meetcampfire.com" if domain == "robinhood.com" else "robinhood.com"
    assert other not in agent.system
    with pytest.raises(sqlguard.GuardError):                     # the full database is not reachable either
        sqlguard.run(agent.conn, "SELECT * FROM companies")

def test_the_command_line_chat_stops_on_exit_or_quit(word, monkeypatch, capsys):
    from leadership import agent as agent_module, cli

    class Fake:

        def __init__(self, *a, **k):
            pass

        def ask(self, question):
            raise AssertionError(f"asked {question!r}")

    monkeypatch.setattr(agent_module, "Agent", Fake)
    monkeypatch.setattr("builtins.input", lambda prompt="": word)
    assert cli.main(["chat", "robinhood.com"]) == 0
    assert "exit, quit" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_a_count_says_what_it_can_miss_when_sources_could_not_be_read():
    from leadership.citations import add_count_note, unread_sources
    unread = unread_sources(FIXTURE, "robinhood.com")
    assert "https://investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership" in unread
    zero = [Step(sql="SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT person) FROM current_leadership WHERE level = 'vp'",

    text = add_count_note("0 vice presidents found in public sources.", zero, "robinhood.com", unread)

    five = [Step(sql="select count(*) from current_leadership", columns=["n"], rows=[[5]])]

    names = [Step(sql="SELECT person FROM current_leadership", columns=["person"], rows=[["A B"]])]
    assert add_count_note("A B.", names, "robinhood.com", unread) == "A B."             # not a count

All four fixes are done on `m5-chat`, each with a regression test in `tests/test_chat.py`. Nothing is committed yet.

To avoid new model calls, I made every change outside `agent.py` and `sqlguard.py`. Those two files feed the chat cache key, so changing them would have discarded all 34 cached answers. The evaluation still scores 31 of 31 with every answer taken from the cache. M5 acceptance passes 6 of 6 (368 fast tests) and the secret scan is clean. That run did include the 2 real-model tests, which make a few model calls each time.

1. **Unrelated sources:** the previous-CFO answer already cited the SEC filing that ended Warnick's role. The code that adds missing sources only checked his main source column, so it also appended a 2020 press release about another executive's hire.
   - A person cited by any of their URLs now gets nothing added.
   - For a former role, the source added is the one that ended it.
   - A surname shared by two people in the results no longer counts as naming either of them.

   The answer now cites 1 URL instead of 2, so the evaluation total dropped from 29 to 28 cited URLs.
2. **Selected company only:** this was already the case, because the agent's snapshot holds only one company's rows. It is now tested for both companies: the other company's people and domain can't be read, the full database tables can't be read, and the prompt doesn't mention the other company. I didn't make the domain argument required in `sqlguard.py`, because that would also discard the cache.
3. **CLI:** `exit`, `quit`, `q` and `bye` now stop the chat, as well as an empty line.
4. **Counts:** "0 vice presidents found in public sources" is now followed by a note. It says the count covers only sources that could be read, that 29 of Robinhood's sources could not be read (15 on its own site), and that finding none doesn't mean there are none. The note is added in code from the database, so it needs no model call and the cache is unaffected.

For your review:
- In [fixtures/citation_review.md](fixtures/citation_review.md), item 4 now shows the corrected answer, and items 3 and 9 show the count note.
- [acceptance/M5.md](acceptance/M5.md) has these fixes as issues 7 to 10, the new numbers, and a new manual test, MT-5.5b. The manual tests now total 11.

The web page doesn't show the count note yet. That needs `m5-chat` merged into `m6-ui` and a one-line change in `app.py`.

"""Streamlit chat over the collected leadership data. SPEC section 5, "UI".

    uv run python -m streamlit run app.py

Reads the committed fixtures (fixtures/leadership.db); needs one LLM key in

and the rows it returned.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

import streamlit as st

from leadership.agent import Agent, collected_on
from leadership.citations import add_missing_sources
from leadership.config import ROOT, ConfigError, configured_providers, load_config, load_env

FIXTURE = ROOT / "fixtures" / "leadership.db"
EXAMPLES = ["Who is the CEO?", "Who are the current C-level executives?",
            "How many C-level executives were found?", "Who was the previous CFO?"]


def companies() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(domain, name) of the companies in the fixtures, read by this page, not by the model."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{FIXTURE.as_posix()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        return conn.execute("SELECT domain, name FROM companies ORDER BY name").fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()

\[REDACTED]_resource(show_spinner=False)
def agent_for(domain: str) -> Agent:
    return Agent(load_config(), domain, FIXTURE)


def rows_table(columns: list[str], rows: list[list]) -> str:
    """The rows as a plain Markdown table. Not st.dataframe: that needs pyarrow's compiled libraries,
    which some machines' security policy blocks."""
    def cell(value) -> str:
        text = "" if value is None else str(value)
        text = text if len(text) <= 160 else text[:157] + "..."
        return text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ").replace("$", "\\$")

    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(columns)]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(cell(v) for v in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def show_answer(entry: dict) -> None:
    text = entry["text"].replace("$", "\\$")           # a dollar sign is not the start of a formula
    if entry["ok"]:
        st.markdown(text)
    else:
        st.error(text)
    with st.expander("SQL and source rows"):
        if not entry["steps"]:
            st.caption("No query ran.")
        for i, step in enumerate(entry["steps"], 1):
            st.code(step.sql or "(empty)", language="sql")
            if step.error:
                st.caption(f"Query {i} was refused or failed: {step.error}")
            elif step.rows:
                st.markdown(rows_table(step.columns, step.rows))
            else:
                st.caption(f"Query {i} returned no rows.")
        st.caption("Answered from the cache." if entry["cached"] else f"Model: {entry['model']}")


def main() -> None:
    st.set_page_config(page_title="Company leadership", page_icon=":material/groups:")
    load_env()
    st.title("Company leadership")
    st.caption("Executive team research from public sources, with the source behind every answer.")
    if not FIXTURE.exists():
        st.error("No data found at fixtures/leadership.db. Run `uv run leadership export` first.")
        return
    options = companies()
    if not options:
        st.error("The database holds no company. Run `uv run leadership collect` and `export` first.")
        return
    with st.sidebar:
        domain = st.selectbox("Company", [d for d, _ in options],
                              format_func=lambda d: dict(options)[d] + f" ({d})")
        st.caption("Answers come only from public sources collected for this company. Each answer has a "
                   "panel with the SQL that ran and the rows behind it.")
        st.markdown("**Try:**\n" + "\n".join(f"- {q}" for q in EXAMPLES))
    if not configured_providers():
        st.error("No LLM key found. Copy .env.example to .env and set GROQ_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, then "
                 "reload this page.")
        return
    try:
        agent = agent_for(domain)
    except ConfigError as e:
        st.error(f"Configuration problem: {e}")
        return
    with st.container(border=True):
        st.markdown(f"**{agent.company}**  ·  {domain}  ·  "
                    f"Data collected {collected_on(FIXTURE, domain) or 'on an unknown date'}  ·  "
                    f"Collection {agent.status.replace('_', ' ')}")
    if agent.status != "complete":
        st.warning(f"The data collection for this company did not finish normally (status {agent.status}). "
                   "Answers are based on partial data.")
    history: list[dict] = st.session_state.setdefault(f"history:{domain}", [])
    for entry in history:
        with st.chat_message("user", avatar=":material/person:"):
            st.markdown(entry["question"])
        with st.chat_message("assistant", avatar=":material/business_center:"):
            show_answer(entry)
    question = st.chat_input(f"Ask about {agent.company}'s leadership")
    if question:
        with st.chat_message("user", avatar=":material/person:"):
            st.markdown(question)
        with st.chat_message("assistant", avatar=":material/business_center:"):
            with st.spinner("Looking it up in the collected data..."):
                result = agent.ask(question)
            entry = {"question": question, "text": add_missing_sources(result.text, result.steps),
                     "ok": result.ok, "steps": result.steps, "cached": result.cached, "model": result.model}
            show_answer(entry)
        history.append(entry)


main()

def ask(self, question: str) -> Answer:
        self.log.event("question", domain=self.domain, question=question, run_status=self.status)
        if self.cache is not None:
            for _provider, model in self.llm.chain:
                hit = self.cache.get(self._cache_key(question, model))
                if hit is not None:
                    answer = Answer(question=question, text=hit["text"], ok=hit["ok"], model=hit["model"],
                                    steps=[Step(**s) for s in hit["steps"]], cached=True)
                    self._log_answer(answer)
                    return answer
        answer = self._loop(question)
        if self.cache is not None and answer.model and answer.ok is not None and not answer.text.startswith(
                "The language model could not be reached"):
            self.cache.put(self._cache_key(question, answer.model),
                           {"text": answer.text, "ok": answer.ok, "model": answer.model,
                            "steps": [asdict(s) for s in answer.steps]})
        self._log_answer(answer)
        return answer

    def _log_answer(self, answer: Answer) -> None:
        self.log.event("answer", question=answer.question, ok=answer.ok, cached=answer.cached, model=answer.model,
                       sql_attempts=len(answer.steps), sql_errors=sum(1 for s in answer.steps if s.error),
                       answer=answer.text)

    def _loop(self, question: str) -> Answer:
        a = self.cfg.agent
        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "system", "content": self.system},
                                {"role": "user", "content": question}]
        steps: list[Step] = []
        errors, model, nudged = 0, None, False
        for _ in range(a.max_steps):
            try:

- Questions the chat must handle: role lookup ("Who's their CTO?"), aggregation
  ("How many VPs?"), department lookup ("Who heads marketing?"), attribute
  lookup ("Where is their CEO based?"), and history ("Who was the previous CFO?").

### Out of scope

- Board-only directors, advisors, investors, directors and managers below VP.
  They may be stored with `level = other` but are excluded from leadership answers.
- Scraping LinkedIn pages. A LinkedIn URL or a search-result snippet may be
  recorded if a search API returns it, but LinkedIn itself is never fetched.
- Authentication, multi-user support, deployment, scheduling of re-collection.
- Vector search, org-chart / reporting-line modelling.
- Tracing services, dashboards, or any infrastructure beyond local files.

### Non-functional requirements

- **Clone-and-go**: with fixtures committed, the chat runs with a single LLM key
  and no collection step.
- **Attribution for every fact**: every stored fact has a source URL and an
  evidence quote that is checked against the source text.
- **Attribution is not truth**: a quote proves the source said it. Whether it
  is believed is decided separately by source reliability, freshness, and
  explicit events (section 3.6).
- **Honest answers**: counts are stated as "found in public sources"; missing
  data is reported as not found; unverified records are labelled.
- **Bounded cost**: every collection run has configurable limits and always
  terminates (section 3.10).
- **Resumable**: an interrupted run continues without repeating finished work
  (section 3.11).
- **Real LLMs only**: no stubs or mocked completions anywhere, including evals.

I checked the code without changing any files or making model calls.

## 1. Database only, or live web search?

The chat only queries the database; it can't search the web.
- The agent has exactly one tool, `query_db(sql)` ([agent.py:28](leadership/agent.py:28)). No search tool is passed to the model ([agent.py:223](leadership/agent.py:223)).
- That tool reads a snapshot of the two views, `leadership` and `current_leadership`, for the selected company only. The snapshot is read-only and holds no other tables ([sqlguard.py](leadership/sqlguard.py)).
- Tavily web search is used only by the collection pipeline (`leadership/collect.py`), never by the chat.

## 2. Out-of-scope questions, such as Robinhood's 2025 revenue

It should answer "not found", but that rests mainly on the prompt, not on code.
- **Prompt rule 1** ([agent.py:79](leadership/agent.py:79)): answer only from the rows, never from general knowledge, and say "not found in the collected data" when the rows don't answer.
- **The rule enforced in code** ([agent.py:236-243](leadership/agent.py:236)): an answer is accepted only after at least one successful query. If the model tries to answer without querying, it is asked once to query. If it still doesn't, the reply is "I could not look this up in the collected data, so I will not answer from memory."
- **What the evaluation shows:**
  - "What is Vlad Tenev's salary?" passed with "I couldn't find Vlad Tenev's salary in the collected Robinhood leadership data", and it gave no figure.
  - In a hallucination test, the CEO was removed from a test copy of the database. The agent answered "not found" and didn't name him from memory.
- **Weak points:**
  - A revenue question isn't in the evaluation, so that exact case is untested. It's the same kind of question as the salary one.
  - The code only checks that some query succeeded, not that it was relevant. Even `SELECT 1` counts. After that, keeping general knowledge out of the answer depends on the model following the prompt. It does so in every evaluated case, but code doesn't guarantee it.

## 3. A new company URL in the page

The page doesn't start a collection, and there is nowhere to enter a URL.
- The "Company" selector lists only the companies already in `fixtures/leadership.db` ([app.py:25](app.py:25), [app.py:85](app.py:85)).
- To add a company, you run the pipeline separately from the command line: `uv run leadership collect <url>`, then `uv run leadership export`. The company then appears in the selector.
- This follows the spec: the chat runs from committed data with one LLM key and no collection step. Collection costs search and model calls and takes minutes, so it isn't triggered from the page.

## 4. Does it meet "LLM-powered chat over the dataset"?

The original take-home brief isn't in the repository, so I checked against SPEC's restatement of it. SPEC section 1 says: "answer natural-language questions over that dataset through a chat interface backed by a real LLM."

**What meets it:**
- A real LLM (Groq first, OpenAI as fallback) writes SQL through a function call, reads the returned rows, and answers with source URLs.
- Both a web page and a CLI are provided.
- The evaluation: 31 of 31 correct; 8 of 8 sample questions; hallucination, injection and incomplete-data tests passed; and your citation review was 10 of 10.

**Caveats to state honestly:**
- **The answers can only be as complete as the data.** For Robinhood the data holds 5 of 11 C-level leaders and 0 of 14 VPs, because its leadership pages refused automated access. The chat now says so on count answers.
- **The no-general-knowledge guarantee** depends on the prompt plus the must-query rule, as described in section 2.
- **Collection is a separate step.** If the brief means a user types a new company's URL into the chat UI, that isn't supported.
- **Status:** M5 and M6 are built but not signed off or merged to `main`, and M7 (README, deliverables, fresh-clone test) hasn't started.

content.text:
The stored data is correct, but the answer isn't. The model attached the wrong URLs and dates to the right rows, and Verma's employment status was never in the rows it requested. Nothing in the code checks any of this, and the M5 citation check couldn't catch it either. I changed nothing and made no model calls. I read the log in `logs/chat-robinhood.com-20261113T225046.jsonl` and reran the agent's SQL on the fixture database.

## What the agent ran and got back

It ran one query, and the model answered after a single round of SQL:

```sql
SELECT person, title, canonical_role, ended_on, end_reported_on, ended_by_source_url,
       ended_by_source_date, source_url, source_type, source_date
FROM leadership WHERE status = 'former' AND department = 'finance'
```

| Row | Role start or seen (`source_url`, `source_date`) | Role end (`ended_on`, `end_reported_on`, `ended_by_source_*`) | `employment_status` (not selected) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warnick, CFO | 2020 Smedley press release, 2020-08-04. It names him as CFO in 2020 | ended_on **2026-02-06**, from the SEC proxy of 2026-04-22 | former |
| Verma, PAO | June 2026 8-K, 2026-06-26 | ended_on **2026-06-25**, from the same 8-K | **current** |
| Verma, SVP Finance and Strategy and Treasurer | Feb 2026 8-K (`hood-20260206.htm`), **2026-02-10** | ended_on empty; end_reported_on **2026-04-22**, from the April proxy ("Prior to his current position…") | **current** |

## Root causes

1. **Wrong source for the end claims (items 1 and 3).** Each former row carries two URLs: where the role was seen, and where its end was seen. Prompt rule 3 says to cite `source_url` for every person, and rule 5 says to cite `ended_by_source_url` for a former role. They conflict, and the model followed rule 3 in both cases. The Smedley release does support "Warnick was CFO in 2020", but not his leaving.
   - My earlier fix doesn't help here. It only adds a source when the answer cites none.
   - The M5 citation check passed this answer. It only checks that each cited URL belongs to someone the answer names, and Warnick is named in the Smedley release. It doesn't check which claim each URL supports.
2. **Role versus company (item 2).** The model's query didn't select `employment_status`, so it never saw that Verma is still at Robinhood as CFO. The rule to distinguish the two is in the prompt only, and nothing makes the model select that column.
3. **Wrong date (item 3).** "2022-02-10" appears nowhere in the rows. It is the model miscopying 2026-02-10, and no code checks dates in answers.
4. **A report date read as an end date (item 3).** `end_reported_on` (2026-04-22) is the date of the proxy that first described the SVP role as past. No source states when that role ended.
   - The answer did say "no exact end date was given", but "reported as ended on 2026-04-22" still reads like an end date.
   - Verma most likely gave up the SVP role when he became CFO on 2026-02-06, but no source states that. I'd keep it as "not stated".

## Proposed fix

**1. Prompt (`agent.py`): turn rules 3 and 5 into a claim-to-source table.**
- "Held the role" cites `source_url` and `source_date`.
- "The role ended" cites `ended_by_source_url` and `ended_by_source_date`, never `source_url`.
- `ended_on` is a stated end date. `end_reported_on` is not: the answer says "end date not stated; first reported as ended in <source>, <date>".
- Every former role also says whether the person is still at the company, and names their current role if the rows have it.
- Dates are copied exactly from the rows.
- The history example query selects `employment_status`.

**2. A check in code (`citations.py`) that doesn't depend on what the model selected.**
- For every former role in the returned rows whose person the answer names, it looks up the full row in the snapshot. It flags these problems:
  - the end source isn't cited, or only the role's start or seen source is;
  - a date in the answer appears in none of the returned rows;
  - the person is still at the company, but the answer doesn't say so;
  - an `end_reported_on` date is presented as an end date.
- If anything is flagged, the model gets one correction turn listing the exact problems, and the answer is checked again. This costs a model call only when a problem is found.
- If problems remain, the answer is shown with a visible warning listing them. It is never silently passed.

**3. Regression tests for this exact question.**
- **Fast, no model:** the exact rows above, plus the bad answer from the log. The check must flag all four problems and must pass a corrected answer.
- **Real model:** asks the exact question and asserts:
  - Warnick cites `hood-20260422.htm`, and the Smedley URL is absent;
  - Verma is described as still at Robinhood, as CFO;
  - no date appears that isn't in the rows;
  - the SVP role's end is given as "not stated", not as 2026-04-22.
- **Evaluation:** the question is added to `fixtures/chat_eval.json`, and the grader uses the same check, so the evaluation can catch this class of error.

## Cost

Any change to `agent.py` invalidates the 34 cached evaluation answers. Re-running the evaluation would make about 100 Groq calls; the new tests add a few. You asked for small runs, so I'd rerun only the new tests and the real-model tests (under 10 calls). The full evaluation rerun would be left until you choose to do it.

I can't make any of this fully reliable with prompt changes alone. That's why the check in code, rather than the prompt, is what catches errors.

content.text:
Here are the five choices that shape the fix, each with my recommendation, so we can settle them first.

**1. Who writes the answer for former roles?**
- **A. The model writes it, code checks it, and the model gets one correction turn.** This is what I proposed. It keeps natural prose, but it is only as reliable as the check, and a correction costs an extra call.
- **B. Code writes the facts for former roles from the rows.** For example: "Jason Warnick: Chief Financial Officer until 2026-02-06 (SEC filing, 2026-04-22: URL). He has left the company." The model only writes the framing, or nothing at all for pure history questions. The source, date and employment status are then correct by construction, with no correction calls. Answers read more like a table, and it is more code.
- **My view:** A is enough if the check is strict. B is the safe option if you want this class of error closed for good. History questions are where all four errors came from.

**2. What if the check still fails after the correction?**
Show the answer with a warning listing the problems, or replace it with code-written facts, as in option B. I lean toward replacing it: a warning still shows wrong text.

**3. Verma's SVP end date.**
No source states it, though he very likely left the SVP role when he became CFO on 2026-02-06. My recommendation is to keep "not stated; first reported as ended in the April 2026 proxy". Inferring the date would break your "no claim without evidence" rule.

**4. How far the check reaches.**
Your four bugs are all about former roles. The same mismatch can happen for current roles, for example citing an old source as the evidence for "currently CFO". My recommendation is to cover former roles now, plus the date check for every answer. A full claim-by-claim check for current roles would be a bigger change.

**5. The evaluation cache.**
Any prompt change invalidates the 34 cached answers. Rerunning the evaluation is about 100 Groq calls. Option B without a prompt change avoids that entirely; option A needs the rerun before M5 can be signed off with current numbers.

My recommendation: B for former roles, the date check on every answer, "not stated" for the SVP end date, and replacing rather than warning. Which way do you want to go on 1 and 5? The others follow from those two.
